items.name: Redis
items.explanation: An in-memory data store, often used as a shared cache or queue. Answers are fast, but everything it holds must fit in memory.

assumedBy.quote: The enqueue handler selects one of the configured Redis hosts based on a hash of this identifier and the logical queue for the given job.

sources.title: Get started with Redis Open Source

items.name: Kafka topics, partitions and offsets
items.explanation: Kafka keeps messages in an ordered log per topic, split into partitions. A reader tracks its place with an offset, so it can resume or replay from any point.

assumedBy.quote: JQRelay relies on Kafka commit offsets to track jobs in each topic partition.

items.name: RPC and Thrift
items.explanation: A remote procedure call lets one service call a function on another as if it were local. Thrift describes those calls in a shared definition and generates the client and server code.

assumedBy.quote: FOQS stores items that live in a topic within a namespace. It exposes a Thrift API

items.name: Circuit breakers
items.explanation: A guard that stops calling a failing part for a while, so failures do not pile up.

assumedBy.quote: FOQS uses a circuit breaker design pattern to mark down shards that are unhealthy.
